# Decompose the `worklist.ts` god class

**File:** `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — 7,823 lines, 89 exported symbols,
20 banner-delimited sections, one 2,260-line function (`runWorklistTui`, 5564–7823).

## Problem statement

`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` carries the entire Herdr work-item selection
experience — constants and maps, the mutable list state machine, row/detail/meta
formatting, tooltip and help rendering, chord and key handling, the mouse input
pipeline, the list renderer, command dispatch and the TUI lifecycle loop — in a
single 7,823-line module. Because the biggest single concern (`runWorklistTui`,
2,260 lines of nested closures over one large mutable context) sits in the same
file as everything else, every change requires holding thousands of unrelated
lines in view, and the blast radius of a diff is not legible from the file it
touches.

This item is the follow-up filed by WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 (producer directive,
intake Q1 → A: *"If any file is >1000 lines it should be evaluated for
refactoring and if appropriate a work item should be created"*). The
downtime-worker decomposition established the pattern this item reuses:
move-only extraction, thin compatibility barrel, tests untouched as the
behaviour gate, sequenced child items.

## Users

- **Herdr UI maintainers (agents and humans)** changing one concern (a key
  binding, the metadata panel, the mouse drag path, the refresh loop) without
  re-reading 7,800 lines.
- **Reviewers/auditors** who need a diff whose blast radius is attributable to
  one module and one test file.
- **Future agents** implementing worklist work items, who need named modules
  locatable by file search instead of a monolith.
- **Operators** who benefit indirectly: smaller modules shorten the review and
  audit cycle for every worklist change.

Example user stories:

- As an agent changing the metadata panel, I want `formatMetadataPanel` and its
  helpers in their own module so that I can verify the change against its own
  tests.
- As a reviewer, I want the key-handling diff to touch only the key-handling
  module so that I can reason about input regressions in isolation.
- As a maintainer, I want every module under 1,000 lines so that any one concern
  is readable in a single pass.
- As a maintainer, I want `runWorklistTui` to be a thin orchestrator over named
  handler modules so that the TUI lifecycle is reviewable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No production file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports
   ≤1,000 for `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (reduced to a thin barrel) and for
   every module created by the split. The single 2,260-line `runWorklistTui`
   function is broken up so no module and no single exported function carries it
   whole.
2. **Public surface preserved — used symbols only.** Every symbol currently
   imported from `./worklist.js` by another module remains exported from that
   exact path with identical types and values, so the 36 importing files
   (2 production consumers + 34 test files, of which 24 are `worklist*.test.ts`
   suites) compile with no import-path edits. 66 distinct symbols are imported
   today; the barrel
   re-exports **only symbols consumers actually use** — unused exports stay
   internal to the extracted modules (inherited producer decision, parent
   WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 intake Q2 → "A, but only re-export symbols that are
   actually used").
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No functional or logic change,
   no renames of public symbols, no behavioural diffs. No test file is modified —
   not its import paths, fixtures or assertions — and all 24 `worklist*.test.ts`
   suites (15,988 lines) plus the whole `packages/herdr` suite pass unchanged.
4. **No new circular imports.** Extracted modules import only from concrete
   sibling modules, never from the `worklist.js` barrel or from `index.ts`; the
   existing `worklist → fetcher/visibility/…` edge direction is preserved and no
   new cycle is introduced.
5. **State ownership is explicit and singular.** The mutable
   `WorkItemListState` (848-line section) and the TUI-local mutable context
   currently closed over by `runWorklistTui` each live in exactly one module;
   extraction must not duplicate mutable state or fork the source of truth.
6. **Responsibility documented per module.** Each new module carries a
   module-level doc comment stating its single responsibility, and existing
   provenance comments (work-item ids, section banners such as
   `// ── Mouse / touch input (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ) ──`) move with their code so
   traceability is preserved.
7. **Testing/validation criterion:** the extracted modules are covered by the
   existing, unmodified `worklist*.test.ts` suites; the split adds no behaviour
   of its own, so no new assertions are required. Validation includes
   `tsc --noEmit`/build success, no new circular-import report, and a line-count
   check asserting every `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` production module is
   ≤1,000 lines.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate code and rewire imports; do not refactor logic,
  improve naming, or "fix" anything encountered on the way (record such findings
  as new work items instead).
- **Barrel compatibility.** 34 files import from `./worklist.js` or
  `./worklist` (including 22 `worklist*.test.ts` suites and the production
  consumers `index.ts` and `fetcher.ts`). The barrel preserves that contract.
- **Sequenced, tree-green landing.** Extract leaf modules first (constants,
  types, layout, formatting) and work inwards towards the state machine and the
  TUI loop, so each merged step leaves the build and the full suite green.
- **`runWorklistTui` is the hard part.** Its 2,260 lines are nested closures
  sharing one large mutable context. The extraction must keep a single context
  object (interface-typed, owned by one module) and pass it explicitly to
  extracted handler functions rather than duplicating state or converting to a
  class-based controller (that would be a behavioural rewrite, not a move).
- **No new runtime dependencies**, no test-file rewrites, no changes to Herdr
  key bindings, shortcuts, rendering output or the `wl` CLI contract.
- **Scope boundary.** This epic targets production modules under
  `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts`. Test files exceeding the ceiling
  (`worklist.test.ts` 7,073 lines, `worklist-mouse.test.ts` 1,132 lines) are
  **out of scope** under the recommended option (see Appendix Q1) and would be
  filed as a follow-up item, because splitting them would violate AC3
  (unmodified tests as the behaviour gate).
- **Other >1,000-line herdr files are out of scope** (tracked separately:
  `index.ts` WL-0MVGKGFFN009UCM6, `fetcher.ts` WL-0MVGKH47T007GKN1,
  `dispatcher-anchor.ts` WL-0MVGKHCP9005SJPZ, `downtime-log.ts`
  WL-0MVGKHFT4003X6JW, `downtime-worker.ts` WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — `runWorklistTui` closure extraction (high).** 2,260 lines of closures
  over shared mutable state; moving them behind an explicit context risks
  behavioural drift in refresh/scheduler/resume-poll ordering. *Mitigation:*
  extract one closure group per child item, keep the context interface-typed and
  single-owner, land each step with the full suite green, and treat
  `worklist*.test.ts` as the gate.
- **Risk — silent re-export drift (medium).** Trimming the barrel to used
  symbols only can break a consumer the search missed (dynamic imports, tests
  using `import *`). *Mitigation:* derive the used-symbol set mechanically from
  the import scan, then verify with `tsc --noEmit` across the package.
- **Risk — cycle formation (medium).** Extracted modules that need shared types
  may reach for `worklist.js` or `index.ts`. *Mitigation:* put shared types in
  `worklist.types.ts` (leaf), and forbid barrel imports from extracted modules
  (AC4), verified by the dependency check.
- **Risk — review fatigue / large diff (medium).** A single big-bang split would
  be unreviewable. *Mitigation:* sequenced child items, leaf-first, one concern
  per child.
- **Risk — scope creep (medium).** The split will surface dead code, duplicated
  helpers and naming oddities. *Mitigation:* record them as new work items;
  do not fix in place.
- **Assumption — test files are out of scope** for the ceiling in this epic
  (Appendix Q1 recommended option A): tests stay unmodified as the behaviour
  gate and the two oversized suites (`worklist.test.ts` 7,073,
  `worklist-mouse.test.ts` 1,132) get a dedicated follow-up item.
- **Assumption — inherited producer decisions** from WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 apply
  unchanged: barrel re-exports used symbols only (Q2), and the epic is delivered
  as sequenced child items in dependency order, one per extracted module (Q3).
- **Assumption — no public API beyond `./worklist.js`** is promised: the
  extracted module paths are internal to `packages/herdr`.

# Refactor: decompose `src/commands/interview.ts` god class

**File:** `src/commands/interview.ts` — 1,630 lines, 41 exports, 9 logical sections.

## Problem statement

`src/commands/interview.ts` carries the whole `wl interview` backend — clarifying-section
detection, Q/A parsing and lossless re-serialisation, the producer-review explanation
(LLM + structured fallback), LLM-assisted question extraction, the interactive walkthrough
loop, readline plumbing and Commander registration — in one 1,630-line module. It breaches
the 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted for WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7, so navigating,
reviewing and safely changing any one concern means holding the whole file in view.

## Users

- **Agents implementing interview/LLM changes** — need one concern (e.g. the answer
  re-serialiser, or the extraction prompt) locatable by file search instead of by reading
  1,630 lines; a monolith inflates context cost and increases the chance of editing the
  wrong helper with a similar name (`cleanQuestion` vs `firstLine` vs `truncateBytes`).
- **Reviewers/auditors** — need a diff whose blast radius is legible from the touched
  module boundary.
- **Producers running `wl interview`** — benefit indirectly: behaviour-preserving
  decomposition lowers the regression risk of every future change to the command.

Example user stories:

- As an agent fixing a Q/A parsing defect, I want the parser and re-serialiser in one
  focused module, so that I can reason about round-trip losslessness without loading the
  LLM and Commander code.
- As a reviewer, I want each extracted module to state one responsibility, so that I can
  judge a diff against a single boundary.
- As a maintainer, I want the `wl interview` command behaviour and the public module
  surface unchanged, so that no test, registry entry or documented flag needs reworking.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Ceiling met.** `src/commands/interview.ts` and every file under `src/interview/` is
   ≤ 1,000 lines (target: largest extracted module ≤ 500). Evidence recorded in the work
   item as `wc -l` output for the module family.
2. **Public surface unchanged.** All 41 current exports of `src/commands/interview.ts`
   (2 section, 4 Q/A, 15 explanation, 11 extraction, 5 loop, 4 registration) plus the
   default `register` export remain importable from the unchanged specifier
   `src/commands/interview.js` with identical names, kinds and signatures; the barrel
   re-exports the full surface. `src/command-registry.ts`
   (`interview: () => import('./commands/interview.js')`) is untouched and needs no edit.
3. **Move-only, behaviour-preserving.** No logic, regex, message, ordering or flag
   changes. Test assertions, fixtures, `describe` titles and mock targets are unmodified;
   the only mechanical test change permitted is the lockstep split of the oversized suite
   `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` (1,696 lines): every resulting file is ≤ 1,000 lines,
   `describe` groups move verbatim and only import paths change. Test count is preserved
   (the split neither adds nor drops a test).
4. **No circular imports, one direction only.** Extracted modules import concrete siblings
   and `../lib/*`, `../config.js`, `../types.js`; **no** `src/interview/*` module imports
   the `src/commands/interview.ts` barrel. The dependency direction is
   `commands/interview.ts` → `interview/*`.
5. **Responsibilities documented.** Every new module carries a one-line module doc comment
   naming its single responsibility, and existing provenance comments/work-item ids
   (`WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67`, `WL-0MUUAMP7M008Z4GK`, `WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF`,
   `WL-0MUX2W8IN005RW66`, `WL-0MUQ0VP800068DNX`) move with their code.
6. **Builds and tests.** `npm run build` (tsc, NodeNext, `rootDir: src`) is green and the
   full project test suite passes via `/skill:test`.
7. **Documentation updated.** All related documentation reflects the changes, including
   code comments, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (command/module map), `CLI.md` if any wording
   drifts, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries. `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded
   (release pipeline).

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate code and update imports only. No "while we're here" rewrites, no
  renames of public symbols, no regex or prompt-text edits. Any incidental improvement
  found en route becomes a separate `discovered-from` work item.
- **Layout: mirror `src/doctor/`.** Helpers for a single command live in a top-level
  feature directory (`src/doctor/*` ← `src/commands/doctor.ts`); this item follows that
  established precedent with `src/interview/*`. The entry file stays
  `src/commands/interview.ts` so the ESM specifier `./commands/interview.js` keeps
  resolving to `dist/commands/interview.js` under NodeNext (a directory-index barrel
  `interview/index.ts` would break that specifier).
- **No new dependencies.** Only existing imports (`../lib/llm.js`,
  `../lib/progress-feedback.js`, `../config.js`, `../mutation-lock.js`, `../types.js`,
  `../cli-types.js`, `readline`) may be used by the extracted modules.
- **No behaviour-parity tooling in scope.** A repo-wide 1,000-line guard is a separate
  open item (WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL, `discovered-from` the sweep); this item verifies the
  ceiling with `wc -l` evidence plus a small structural assertion (see Risks).
- **Escaped backticks** only in written content; Markdown otherwise.

## Existing state

`src/commands/interview.ts` — 1,630 lines, 41 exports, single default `register`, no
module-level mutable state (only `const` regexes/constants). Section map (current `dev`):

| Lines | Section | Exports |
|---|---|---|
| 1–70 | File doc comment + imports | — |
| 71–116 | Section markers (regexes, `INSERT_WRAPPER`) | — (all private) |
| 117–160 | Section extraction | `ClarifyingSection`, `extractClarifyingSection` |
| 161–564 | Q/A parsing and re-serialisation | `ClarifyingQAPair`, `parseQAPairs`, `rebuildQAPairs`, `rebuildDescription` |
| 565–873 | Producer-review explanation | 15 (caps, context/deps types, prompt, render, fallback, LLM result) |
| 874–1052 | LLM-assisted question extraction | 11 (instruction, caps, prompt, parser, result, extract fns, section insert/merge) |
| 1053–1260 | Core interview loop | `InterviewStore`, `InterviewIO`, `InterviewOutcome`, `InterviewRunOptions`, `runInterview` |
| 1261–1291 | Interactive input | — (`createPromptLoop` private) |
| 1292–1630 | Types + command registration | `InterviewPromptLoop`, `InterviewCommandDeps`, `defaultClearPrompt`, `register` (default) |

Consumers: exactly one production importer — `src/command-registry.ts` (dynamic import,
default export only) — and one test file, `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` (1,696 lines, 19
top-level `describe` blocks, no `vi.mock`, imports 11 named exports + default). No file in
`src/`, `packages/`, `scripts/` or `bench/` imports any other symbol from the module, and
no documentation references the file path.

## Desired change

Extract cohesive modules under `src/interview/`, leaving `src/commands/interview.ts` as the
command entry (registration + interactive plumbing) **and** the public barrel. Proposed map
(export attribution is exhaustive — every current export belongs to exactly one row):

| Module | Responsibility | Exports moved | Est. lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/commands/interview.ts` (entry + barrel) | Commander registration, `register` action flow, prompt loop, deps surface, re-export of the full public surface | `InterviewPromptLoop`, `InterviewCommandDeps`, `defaultClearPrompt`, `register` (default) + all re-exports | ~400 |
| `src/interview/section.ts` | Clarifying-section heading detection and extraction | `ClarifyingSection`, `extractClarifyingSection` | ~95 |
| `src/interview/qa.ts` | Q/A parsing, answer-region computation and lossless re-serialisation | `ClarifyingQAPair`, `parseQAPairs`, `rebuildQAPairs`, `rebuildDescription` | ~400 |
| `src/interview/explanation.ts` | Producer-review explanation: evidence formatting, prompt, render, structured fallback, LLM call | 15 exports | ~310 |
| `src/interview/extraction.ts` | LLM-assisted question extraction plus canonical-section insert/merge | 11 exports | ~200 |
| `src/interview/loop.ts` | Interactive walkthrough: prompt/persist answers, outcome accounting | `InterviewStore`, `InterviewIO`, `InterviewOutcome`, `InterviewRunOptions`, `runInterview` | ~220 |

Dependency direction after extraction:
`commands/interview.ts` → {section, qa, explanation, extraction, loop} →
{`../lib/llm.js`, `../lib/progress-feedback.js`, `../config.js`, `../types.js`} and
sibling modules only. `loop.ts` → `section.ts`, `qa.ts`, `extraction.ts`;
`extraction.ts` → `qa.ts`, `section.ts`. No module imports the entry barrel (AC4).

### Proposed child decomposition (structural slices)

1. **Foundation** — create `src/interview/` and extract `section.ts` + `qa.ts` (the pure,
   dependency-free parsing core). Blocks the rest.
2. **`explanation.ts`** — largest LLM cluster; independent of the loop.
3. **`extraction.ts`** — depends on `qa.ts`/`section.ts` for insert/merge helpers.
4. **`loop.ts`** — core walkthrough; depends on slices 1 and 3.
5. **Closeout** — thin the entry barrel (`src/commands/interview.ts`), lockstep split of
   `tests/cli/interview.test.ts`, module-map documentation, `wc -l` evidence, build +
   full suite.

Slices are ordered so slice 1 blocks the rest and each slice is independently move-only and
verifiable with the changed-scope test gate.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/interview.ts` — becomes entry + barrel; loses ~1,200 lines, keeps `register`
- `src/interview/section.ts` — new (heading detection/extraction)
- `src/interview/qa.ts` — new (parse/rebuild)
- `src/interview/explanation.ts` — new (producer-review explanation)
- `src/interview/extraction.ts` — new (LLM extraction + section insert/merge)
- `src/interview/loop.ts` — new (interactive walkthrough)
- `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` — split in lockstep into `tests/cli/interview/*.test.ts`
  (parsing/rebuild, loop + extraction, command integration, command `--llm`/progress,
  explanation), assertions verbatim
- `src/command-registry.ts` — read-only (specifier must keep resolving)
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — command/module map note for the new `src/interview/` modules
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `docs/design/incremental-sync.md`, `CLI.md` — read-only
  unless wording names the module layout (it does not today; verify, do not churn)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Silent behaviour drift in the re-serialiser** (the lossless round-trip is the command's
  subtle core; regexes are shared between parsing and rebuild). *Mitigation:* extract
  `qa.ts` first with zero edits, keep the 19 existing `describe` groups untouched, and land
  each slice as a separate move-only commit so a regression is bisectable.
- **Barrel/ESM resolution break.** `src/commands/interview.ts` must keep existing so
  `dist/commands/interview.js` is emitted; a `interview/index.ts` barrel would silently
  break the lazy registry. *Mitigation:* AC2 + the `lazy-command-registry` and
  `entry-point-split` suites as the oracle.
- **Circular imports** if `loop.ts` or `extraction.ts` reach back into the entry for types
  or helpers. *Mitigation:* AC4 — modules import siblings and `../lib/*` only; shared types
  live with their owning module (`section.ts`, `qa.ts`, `loop.ts`).
- **Test-file split churn.** 19 `describe` groups currently share one module scope.
  *Mitigation:* move groups verbatim; add no shared helper unless two target files need the
  same fixture, and then only a mechanical extraction.
- **Regrowth repeats.** This sweep already has a "completed" decomposition that never
  landed (see Related work). *Mitigation within scope:* documented single-responsibility
  module headers; the repo-wide guard is WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL (separate, low priority).
- **Scope creep risk.** The split invites opportunistic "while we're here" cleanups — a
  parser rewrite, prompt-tuning, a new `--flag`, splitting the 266-line `register` action
  into sub-commands. *Mitigation:* AC3 forbids logic edits; any such opportunity is filed
  as a separate item linked `discovered-from:WL-0MVGKGXN80006V9P` rather than absorbed.
- **Review fatigue on a wide-but-shallow diff.** A move-only refactor touches many files
  for zero behavioural gain, which can invite under-review. *Mitigation:* one concern per
  commit/slice, `git diff --color-moved` for reviewers, and the unchanged suites as the
  behaviour oracle.
- **Assumption:** the 1,000-line ceiling applies to non-test source, and to a test file only
  when it is touched in lockstep with its module (sweep rule; identical to
  WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT AC3).
- **Assumption:** the full 41-symbol public surface is retained in the barrel rather than
  trimmed to the 12 symbols tests import. Trimming would be a breaking change for any
  external plugin consumer and buys nothing here; the barrel re-export is ~10 lines.
- **Assumption:** no consumer call-site changes are acceptable — `src/command-registry.ts`
  and the CLI help output must be byte-identical for `wl interview`.
- **Assumption:** no behavioural improvement is bundled; opportunities observed en route
  become separate `discovered-from` items.

## Related work

- WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 — parent sweep/directive: every production file > 1,000 lines is
  evaluated for decomposition (producer Q1 answered).
- WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT — sibling from the same sweep (`packages/shared/src/database.ts`);
  source of the lockstep test-split rule reused in AC3 and the module-map layout pattern
  (entry façade + cohesive modules + explicit dependency direction).
- WL-0MULI1N1N0001WRD — "CLI: Explanation path & new options" (completed); introduced the
  `--no-llm`/`--json` modes and the producer-review explanation path extracted here. (The
  seed description labelled this item "Interview LLM fallback"; the title above is the
  accurate one — the LLM *extraction* fallback is WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF.)
- WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67 ("Interview replay feature"), WL-0MUUAMP7M008Z4GK ("r-i interview
  explanation does not state why an item needs producer review"), WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF
  ("interview: LLM-assisted question extraction as fallback"), WL-0MUX2W8IN005RW66
  ("Feedback in interview when running LLM"), WL-0MUQ0VP800068DNX ("Interview LLM config
  schema") — all completed; provenance items for the behaviour implemented in this file,
  cited in its doc comments and moving with their code.
- WL-0MUQ0VQ8A002HHFA — "Interview LLM fallback integration" (completed); the integration
  work behind the extraction fallback path extracted here.
- WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL — proposed repo-wide file-size guard (`discovered-from` the sweep);
  the reason this item's ceiling check is manual plus a small structural assertion.
- WL-0MVGKH6Z1000XWGJ, WL-0MVGKH9Z900178UF, WL-0MVGKH47T007GKN1, WL-0MVGKHCP9005SJPZ,
  WL-0MVGKHFT4003X6JW — companion god-class items from the same sweep (`init.ts`,
  `github-sync.ts`, `fetcher.ts`, `dispatcher-anchor.ts`, `downtime-log.ts`).
- Repo precedent for layout: `src/doctor/*` helper modules consumed by
  `src/commands/doctor.ts`.

## Appendix: decision log (agent-proposed; producer may override)

No producer interview questions were required: the seed context (goal, drafted ACs, parent
directive) plus two completed sibling intakes from the same sweep answer every open choice,
and all decisions below are reversible at plan/implement time. Recorded for review.

- **Q: Where should the extracted modules live?**
  **Recommended and chosen: `src/interview/`, mirroring the existing `src/doctor/`
  precedent** (top-level feature directory consumed by one command module). The entry stays
  `src/commands/interview.ts` so the ESM specifier `./commands/interview.js` keeps
  resolving under NodeNext.
  Alternatives considered: (b) flat siblings `src/commands/interview-*.ts` (works, but mixes
  six command-specific helpers into the already crowded flat `src/commands/` namespace);
  (c) a `src/commands/interview/index.ts` barrel (breaks the emitted
  `dist/commands/interview.js` specifier the lazy registry depends on).

- **Q: How granular should the split be?**
  **Recommended and chosen:** five extracted modules plus the entry (map above), one per

  inventing new boundaries mid-move.
  Alternatives considered: a two-way split (parsing vs everything else ≈ 470 / 1,150 lines —

- **Q: Keep the full 41-symbol barrel, or trim to the 12 symbols tests import?**
  **Recommended and chosen: keep the full surface.** The parent epic's "used symbols only"

  genuinely internal; here every symbol is a documented part of this command module's

- **Q: Split the oversized test suite in this item?**

- **Q: Add a file-size regression guard here?**

# Decompose the `src/commands/doctor.ts` god class

**File:** `src/commands/doctor.ts` (1,658 lines at intake time; 1,582 when the item was created)

## Problem statement

`src/commands/doctor.ts` is a single 1,658-line module that carries the entire
`wl doctor` CLI surface: six module-level notice/formatting helpers at the top
and eleven command registrations (root `doctor` validation, `upgrade`,
`stage-sync`, `prune`, `cache`, `foreign-items`, `audit-gaps`,
`dangling-parents`, `priority`, `file-paths`, `migrate`), each with its own
inline `async` action body. The `--fix` interactive flow and the findings
aggregation of the root command alone occupy ~385 lines inside one nested
callback. Navigating, reviewing or changing one subcommand requires holding the
other ten in view, so every doctor change carries avoidable regression risk and
the file sits above the 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted for
WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7.

## Users

- **CLI maintainers (agents and humans)** need to change one doctor subcommand
  (e.g. `prune`, `file-paths`, the `--fix` prompt) without reasoning about
  1,600 unrelated lines.
- **Reviewers/auditors** need a diff attributable to a single subcommand so the
  blast radius of a change is legible.
- **Future agents implementing doctor work items** (e.g. the open
  WL-0MVM8V79C003XH2J `wl doctor prefix` item) need a named, findable module
  per subcommand instead of appending to a monolith.

Example user stories:

- As an agent adding a new doctor subcommand, I want an existing per-subcommand
  module template so that registration is mechanical and reviewable.
- As a reviewer, I want a `prune` change to touch only the prune module and its
  tests so that I can verify it against its own suite.
- As a maintainer, I want every doctor file under 1,000 lines so that it is
  readable in a single pass.

1. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports ≤1,000 for
   `src/commands/doctor.ts` (now a thin registrar) and for every module created
   by the split.
2. **Public entry point unchanged.** `src/commands/doctor.ts` still provides
   `export default function register(ctx: PluginContext): void`, so
   `src/command-registry.ts` (`doctor: () => import('./commands/doctor.js')`)
   and every existing CLI test import path keep working with **no importer
   edits**.
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No change to subcommand names,
   flags, help text, human output strings, JSON payload shapes or exit codes; no
   existing test file is modified (import paths, fixtures or assertions), and
   all existing `doctor` CLI/integration tests (`tests/cli/doctor-*.test.ts`,
   `tests/doctor-*.test.ts`) pass unmodified.
4. **One concern per module.** Each extracted module registers exactly one
   doctor subcommand — or, for the shared notices module, one cohesive
   cross-cutting concern — carries a module-level doc comment stating its single
   responsibility, and moves its provenance comments (work-item ids) with the
   code.
5. **No cycles, narrow seams.** Extracted modules never import from
   `src/commands/doctor.ts`; the registrar passes a narrow typed context
   (`program`/`output`/`utils` and `dataPath` only where needed) so handlers do
   not depend on the full `PluginContext` surface.
6. **Line-count guard test (additive).** A new test asserts the doctor module
   family stays at or under 1,000 lines per file and fails when any module
   exceeds the ceiling (mirrors the `downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts`
   precedent from WL-0MVLIHWOY003IP5E — no existing test is touched).
7. **Documentation updated.** Any repository notes that describe the doctor
   command layout (e.g. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CLI.md`, `docs/migrations.md`
   references) remain accurate, and the new module layout is stated in the
   top-of-file doc comment of `src/commands/doctor.ts`.

  root validation/`--fix` action last, so every intermediate state builds and

## Summary

Add a `wl doctor prefix` subcommand that changes the configured project prefix in `.worklog/config.yaml` and renumbers every existing work item to the new prefix, preserving each item's suffix (e.g. `OSL-0MVK31VYQ007CN37` → `CC-0MVK31VYQ007CN37`). The flow must ask for confirmation before it changes anything, default to a read-only preview, and emit a machine-readable rename map.

## Motivation

Requested from the ContentCreator project (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator`), whose configured prefix is `OSL` while the project is now branded `CC`. 1207 work items carry the `OSL-` prefix, and `wl doctor foreign-items` correctly classifies any item whose prefix differs from `.worklog/config.yaml` as foreign — so editing the prefix by hand would make the whole backlog look foreign and break cross-project lookups.

## Scope (proposed)

- `wl doctor prefix` — read-only preview: current prefix, counts of items/comments/dependency edges/audit records, and sample renames.
- `wl doctor prefix --to <PREFIX>` — declare the target prefix (validated: non-empty, no `-`, ASCII alphanumeric).
- `wl doctor prefix --to <PREFIX> --confirm` — apply: rewrite the config prefix, then rewrite every ID-bearing record (`workitems.id`, parent references, dependency edges, comments' `workItemId`, audit results, waivers, and any other ID column), and write a rename map (`osl→cc` pairs) to `.worklog/prefix-rename-<timestamp>.json`.
- Confirmation gate: interactive run without `--confirm` prompts and requires an explicit `y`; a non-TTY run without `--confirm` aborts with no writes and a non-zero exit.
- Idempotent: re-running after a successful rename reports a no-op.
- `--json` output for scripting.
- Docs: `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` and `CLI.md`.

## Acceptance criteria (draft)

- [ ] `wl doctor prefix` (preview) reports counts and sample renames and changes nothing; covered by unit and temp-store integration tests.
- [ ] `--confirm` rewrites every ID-bearing record (items, parents, dependency edges, comments, audit results, waivers) and writes the rename map.
- [ ] Confirmation gate: non-interactive without `--confirm` aborts with a non-zero exit and zero writes; interactive requires explicit `y`.
- [ ] Re-running after a successful rename is a no-op, and a mid-run failure leaves the store recoverable (transactional or a documented rollback).
- [ ] `wl doctor foreign-items` reports zero foreign items after a confirmed rename.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated (CLI.md, DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md, code comments).

## Problem

The test-run cache (`run_tests.py` + `test_cache.py`) can serve a **stale** result, and can also report **missing** for an entry that was just written. Both were observed in one session (WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A). Root cause undiagnosed — the symptoms below contradict `compute_git_state`'s documented content-sensitive fingerprint, so the fingerprint itself may be captured at the wrong moment.

Discovered during WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A (discovered-from).

## Symptom 1 — a stale GREEN was returned for a changed tree

While validating RED witnesses for the peer-offer cooldown work:

1. Production fix applied (5 dirty files) → `run_tests.py --scope changed --group herdr --json` → `Test Files 130 passed`.
2. Production changes reverted (`git checkout -- <3 prod files>`; 2 dirty test files) → the same command → **130 passed / 4007 tests**, i.e. the RED witnesses "passed" without the fix.
3. The same command again, after adding `console.log` diagnostics to those same two test files, **reused the same cache directory** (`metadata.json` `completed_at` unchanged) — a cache hit, despite the file contents having changed.
4. `--no-cache` produced the expected **4 failures**, confirming the RED witnesses were valid.

## Symptom 2 — `--summary` reports `missing` for an entry just stored

Immediately after `run_tests.py --scope full --json` finished green at HEAD (`Test Files 280 passed | 1 skipped`, `Tests 4102 passed | 5 skipped`, cache dir `ada07d39…` with `scope: full`, `test_type: full`, `exit_code: 0`), `run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` (with and without `--scope full`) reported `{"scopes":{"all":"missing"}}`. The checkout was clean at the same HEAD; `compute_git_state()` returned `2838fdc3…` while the stored entry held `6155836a…` — so the entry was keyed on a *transient* dirty state that existed during the run (plugin/`wl`/`dist`/test-created files) and can never be queried again afterwards.

## Impact

- A RED/GREEN verification can be silently wrong — exactly the evidence an audit consumes.
- `implement.py finish`'s changed-scope gate can pass on a stale cached run.
- The audit's `query_cached()` fast path misses for the same reason, forcing an unnecessary full-suite re-execution (F3).
- Agents are likely to trust the green summary and never use `--no-cache`.

## Proposed direction (for intake)

- Make the fingerprint stable for the *state an operator/agent can reproduce*: exclude ignored/transient paths (`.worklog/`, `dist/`, test scratch dirs) from the dirty-path content hash, or snapshot the state before the run rather than after.
- Re-check the content-hash path for `--scope changed` runs (symptom 1) — the file list may be reused where the content hash is not.
- Surface `cached: true` prominently in human-readable output so a re-used result is never mistaken for a fresh one.
- Document/automate: verification runs that must prove RED/GREEN should use `--no-cache`.

## Acceptance criteria (draft)

- Editing only the contents of an already-modified file invalidates the cache entry for that scope/group.
- A run's entry is queryable by `--summary` immediately afterwards from a clean checkout at the same HEAD.
- A cached result is visibly marked as cached in non-JSON output.
- Regression tests: (a) two runs with a content-only change between them do not share a cache entry; (b) `--summary` finds the entry written by the preceding `--scope full` run.

## Goal

**As** a producer or agent scanning the herdr worklist, **I want** each work item to show who holds it — an `Assignee` metadata row plus an `[assignee]` prefix on the item's title — **so that** I can tell a producer hold (`Map`) or an active agent claim apart from an unheld item at a glance, without opening the item or running `wl show`.

## Background

`assignee` is the claim/scheduling-hold field (see `AGENTS.md`: the producer sentinel is `wl update <id> --assignee Map`, released with `--assignee ""`; claim tiers write the agent name). It is already present end-to-end in the data layer — `wl show` / `wl list --json` return it and `normalizeItem` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) parses it into `WorkItem.assignee` — but the herdr TUI never displays it. The `wl show` CLI already renders an `Assignee` row, so the CLI is out of scope.

Related work (not duplicates): WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR surfaces the *aggregate* "entire dispatch window held" banner (header count + warning banner), and WL-0MVAMS4RO000H3B0 restored the per-item `Reviewed` metadata row + list icon — the closest precedent for this shape of change (shared `buildMetaRows` row, list/preview/detail parity, `noIcons` mode, README docs).

## Surfaces

- **Preview** — the selection-list metadata panel (`buildMetadataPanelLines` → `buildMetaRows`) and the hover tooltip.
- **Detail view** — the full item view (`formatDetailContent`: header title + shared metadata table).
- **List rows** — `formatItemLine` (selection list, browse feed and log-derived dispatch rows all render through it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `buildMetaRows` returns an `Assignee` row carrying the item's raw assignee value whenever `assignee` is a non-empty, non-whitespace string, positioned immediately after the `Effort` row so `pairMetaRows` compound pairing (Status+Stage, Priority+Type, Created+Updated, Audit+AuditedAt) can never absorb or reorder it; the row is omitted entirely when `assignee` is undefined, null, empty or whitespace-only.
- AC2: One shared helper (`formatTitleWithAssignee` in `worklist.format.ts`) returns `[<assignee>] <title>` for an assigned item and the byte-identical title for an unassigned one, and every title-rendering surface uses it: selection-list rows (`formatItemLine`), the preview metadata `Title` row, the detail-view header, and the hover-tooltip title line.
- AC3: Unassigned parity — for an item with no assignee every surface renders exactly as today: no `[] ` prefix, no leading space, no empty `Assignee` row, and the existing herdr suites pass unchanged.
- AC4: Rendering invariants hold — list rows still truncate within `maxCols` (display-width aware), the `[assignee] ` prefix inherits the title's priority colour, `noIcons` mode is unaffected, and `metadataPanelContentHeight` counts the extra row so the panel's `m`/`M` scroll clamp can still reach it.
- AC5: Visibility of a real hold — an item with `assignee: "Map"` renders `[Map]` before its title in the list row, the preview `Title` row and the detail header, and `Assignee  Map` in the preview panel and detail metadata table.
- AC6: `packages/herdr/README.md` documents the new `Assignee` row and the `[assignee]` title prefix in its metadata-panel, detail-view and hover-tooltip sections.
- AC7: Test-first — every AC above is covered by a failing test in the herdr vitest suite before the implementation lands, and the full gate is run through `/skill:test`.

## Minimal implementation

1. **Test (red first).** Extend the existing herdr suites (`worklist.test.ts`, `worklist-icon-truncation.test.ts`, `worklist-child-coverage.test.ts`) with: assigned/unassigned `buildMetaRows` + `pairMetaRows` cases, `formatTitleWithAssignee` unit cases, assigned/unassigned `formatItemLine`, `formatDetailContent` header, `formatTooltipLines`, and `metadataPanelContentHeight` accounting.
2. **Helper.** Add `formatTitleWithAssignee(item)` (or `(title, assignee)`) to `worklist.format.ts` — the leaf formatting module — so `worklist.ts` (the not-yet-split monolith under the ≤1000-line shrink-only allowlist) does not grow logic.
3. **Metadata row.** Add the `Assignee` row to `buildMetaRows` after `Effort`, and route the `Title` row through the helper — this covers the preview panel and the detail table in one change.
4. **Title surfaces.** Use the helper in `formatItemLine` (inside the priority-coloured segment) and `formatTooltipLines`, and in the `formatDetailContent` header.
5. **Docs.** Update the README's Metadata panel / detail view / hover tooltip bullets and the `Metadata panel` reference section.

## Plan

Single vertical slice (code + tests + docs); effort Extra Small and risk Low, so no phasing and no prototype is warranted. Between-phase guidance is not applicable — the change is one slice through the shared formatter, its four render call sites, tests and docs.

## Out of scope

- herdr **pane titles** (`pane-title.ts`): load-bearing for active-pane detection via work-item ID matching and width-bounded; adding an assignee prefix would risk truncating the ID.
- The `wl show` / `wl list` CLI output — it already renders `Assignee`.
- `Blocked By` rows: they display *other* items' titles and carry no assignee data.
- Dispatch, claim, sorting and filtering behaviour: this is display-only.

## Assumptions

- A1: "preview and detail views" means the herdr selection-list metadata panel and the full detail view; "the title for the item" means every surface that renders the item's title (list row, preview `Title` row, detail header, hover tooltip).
- A2: the `Assignee` value renders as plain text (no icon — `@worklog/shared/icons` has no assignee icon), and the `[assignee]` prefix inherits the row/title priority colour.
- A3: a whitespace-only assignee is treated as unassigned.
- A4: the change is display-only — no dispatch, claim, sort or filter behaviour changes.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.format.ts` — new `formatTitleWithAssignee` helper (leaf formatting module)
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.meta.ts` — `Assignee` row + `Title` row prefix (preview panel and detail table)
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.detail.ts` — detail-view header title prefix
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `formatItemLine` and `formatTooltipLines` use the helper
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-icon-truncation.test.ts` — width/ANSI and parity tests
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — metadata row, list row, detail and tooltip tests
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — surface documentation

## Appendix: planning decisions and assumptions

No clarifying question was raised: this item was dispatched with effort **Extra Small** and risk **Low** (below the planning threshold), so the plan-skill skip path performed an automated review of the existing content instead of decomposing it, and the item text plus the repository analysis below resolved every point the plan needs. Evidence: `worklist.meta.ts` (`buildMetaRows`), `worklist.detail.ts` (`formatDetailContent`), `worklist.ts` (`formatItemLine`, `formatTooltipLines`). Recorded as assumption A1; callable out at review.

Nearest neighbours: WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR (aggregate hold banner) and WL-0MVAMS4RO000H3B0 (restore `Reviewed` row/icon). No overlap covering these ACs, so nothing was closed or rewritten.
- D4: Structural constraint — new logic goes into `worklist.format.ts` rather than `worklist.ts`, which is under the shrink-only ≤1000-line allowlist in `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/worklist-family.ts`.
- D5: No prototype needed — pure string formatting over an already-populated field.
